details.description: Nova-2 is Deepgram's general-purpose speech-to-text model, built with "speech-specific optimizations to the underlying Transformer architecture, advanced data curation techniques, and a multi-stage training methodology" over its Nova-1 predecessor. Deepgram's Models & Languages Overview lists nova-2 (general) separately from the "Legacy Models" section that groups Nova 1, Enhanced and Base, though Deepgram now offers a newer Nova-3 model above it, recommending Nova-2 for languages Nova-3 does not yet support.
advantages: Deepgram reports an 18.4% reduction in word error rate (WER) from Nova-1.
Deepgram reports a 22.6% relative improvement in punctuation accuracy and a 31.4% relative improvement in capitalization error rate over Nova-1.
Deepgram reports a median WER of 8.4% across all domains and files it tested overall.
Supports a broad set of languages including Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Spanish, per Deepgram's language documentation.
disadvantages: Deepgram positions its newer Nova-3 model above Nova-2, recommending Nova-2 mainly for use cases and languages Nova-3 does not yet support.
use_cases: Transcription in languages not yet supported by Deepgram's newer Nova-3 model.
Filler-word identification, per Deepgram's model recommendation guidance.

sources.title: Nova-2: Automatic Speech Recognition, Reinvented | Deepgram

notes: Treated 'nova-2' as Deepgram's Nova-2-General model, distinct from its specialized nova-2-meeting/phonecall/etc. variants, which are separate catalog entries. WER is lower-is-better so Deepgram's WER figures are reported as advantages, not in evaluations (which requires higher-is-better 0-100 scores); no such maker score was found for Nova-2, so evaluations is left empty. Deepgram's own blog also claims WER improvements over unnamed 'competitors' and over OpenAI Whisper-large, which were not included here since they are comparative marketing claims rather than a single reproducible score. The catalog carries no deprecation_date. Verify pass: the nova-2/nova-2-general row of developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview also lists Greek and Hungarian, which the original list omitted; added them from the same already-cited source.
